sources.overall_mod_summary: Horizon Signal is a rare, long cosmic-horror science-fiction event chain about an artificial black-hole signal, the Worm-in-Waiting, temporal recursion, and consequences that can alter an empire's founder species.
sources.event_chain_summary: A scientist investigates a signal from a black hole. The signal presents GRAVITY IS DESIRE and TIME IS SIGHT, leads to the Exit Point, and repeatedly draws scientists into a causal loop. The chain branches between sending people, destroying the ship, or ending contact; later research leads to Entropic Recursion, the Loop Temple, Doctrine: Strange Loop, Omega Theory, and the Omega Alignment.
trigger_contract: At new game start, the page states a 20% chance for activation in a random uncontrolled black-hole system.
The Infinity Machine and Dimensional Horror systems cannot trigger the event.
The initial event requires a manned science ship with a scientist entering the correct black-hole system; Gestalt Consciousness and Nomadic empires are excluded.
The event cannot happen to AI empires.
Founder-species trait changes remove incompatible traits, including traits that may otherwise be superior.

outcomes: A buried volcanic-rock temple with a Möbius-looped serpent is found.
Investigate the Loop Temple special project is issued.

branches: Pilgrimage: Loop Temple Pilgrims' Way and +10% happiness, plus Doctrine: Strange Loop.
Open to the public: Loop Temple Visitor Center and +5% happiness, plus Doctrine: Strange Loop.

optional_chains.title: The Messenger
optional_chains.availability: After the initial chain and before Omega Alignment is constructed; requires Doctrine: Strange Loop.
optional_chains.summary: A looping escape pod contains a Messenger whose remains resemble the founder species. Research can lead to a reconstructed Messenger and retroviral changes to founder pops, with ethics, traits, and purge or control branches.

optional_chains.title: A Rendezvous
optional_chains.availability: After Doctrine: Strange Loop and before Omega Alignment; requires an existing commander.
optional_chains.summary: The impossible Syzygy appears with a commander who is alive elsewhere. Destroying it can leave the commander foredoomed to a rendezvous, or produce an interference/debris outcome if the commander dies.

optional_chains.title: The Coils of God
optional_chains.availability: After Doctrine: Strange Loop and before Omega Alignment; requires an observation post over a post-Renaissance civilization.
optional_chains.summary: A pre-FTL religious-artistic movement treats clocks, serpents, and looping time as sacred. Observation, suppression, intervention, or participation can produce research, progress, persecution, or the disappearance of the planet's population and the science team.

optional_chains.title: The Waiting World
optional_chains.availability: After Doctrine: Strange Loop and before Omega Alignment; begins when a new planet is colonized with the related features.
optional_chains.summary: A colony discovers abandoned facilities and then impossible population records. Keeping or demolishing the buildings branches into extra pops, disappearance, investigation, quarantine, purge, and physics/Entropic Recursion research.

omega_alignment.building: Omega Alignment on the empire capital
branches: Generate an Entry Point and consent to the Worm: the capital system is transformed and the achievement may be granted.
Generate an Entry Point but refuse: the Worm appears as a Dimensional Horror; defeating it leads to THE SHATTERED LOOP and its rewards.
omega_alignment.theme: The chain resolves the time-loop motif by making the Worm's beginning and end part of the same causal structure.

translation_contract: Keep named entities and research terms consistent across the whole chain.
Preserve causal direction: a choice or completed special project determines the next event; do not collapse THE WORM, - MESSAGE ENDS -, I'M THROUGH, and AN INTERVENTION.
Keep the distinction between main-chain events, optional events, and Omega Alignment events.
Do not turn narrative possibility or atmosphere into unsupported mechanical certainty.

sources.page_title: Quest for the Toxic God events
sources.version_or_revision: The page is for the PC version and states that at least some older sections were last verified for version 3.13; no revision ID/date was exposed in the retrieved view.
sources.user_accuracy_assertion: 玲珑 states that the chain has not materially changed in the recent versions and that the Wiki information is accurate; this is recorded separately from page metadata.
sources.dlc_scope: The page states that the content is available only with the Toxoids DLC enabled.
sources.overall_mod_summary: The Quest for the Toxic God is a multi-stage knightly search story in which the Order pursues a deity through lost knights, Sinople's encrypted records, Shroud bargains, trials, the Trickster, and a final encounter with a toxic spacefaring entity.
sources.event_chain_summary: The situation advances through eight numbered quests. The first follows a banished knight who finds the sentient ship AI Sinople and returns with a clue. Later quests follow multiple knights and supernatural or technological tests, culminating in a returned legendary knight, a confrontation with the Trickster, the opening of a blocked route, and the discovery of a Toxic Entity. The final events branch between defeating or losing the entity, then resolve the Order's purpose and the unanswered distinction between the entity and the true Toxic God.

quest_progression.trigger: Quest for the Toxic God: Stage 2
quest_progression.theme: Banishment, survival, and the first tangible clue
events: The Tale of Knight [Knight 1]: The Nebula
The Tale of Knight [Knight 1]: The Sage
The Tale of Knight [Knight 1]: The Fey
quest_progression.causal_summary: Knight 1 is banished, follows coordinates, survives an abandoned station and a hostile encounter, meets the sentient AI Sinople, and returns. Sinople's records point toward entities resembling the Toxic God; the Order restores Knight 1's status and keeps the clue.
quest_progression.branching_notes: Sinople contains refusal/acceptance and lethal-response choices; preserve whether the AI is treated as a sentient ally or an enemy.

quest_progression.trigger: Quest for the Toxic God: Stage 3
quest_progression.theme: Two knights search for a missing partner
events: The Tale of Knights [A] and [B]: Departure
The Tale of Knights [A] and [B]: The Search
The Tale of Knights [A] and [B]: Milvaunis
The Tale of Knights [A] and [B]: The Finding
quest_progression.causal_summary: Knights A and B follow a long-delayed clue and investigate Milvaunis in search of the missing knight and a route toward the deity.
quest_progression.branching_notes: Keep Knight A, Knight B, and any found or missing knight as distinct roles; do not normalize them to generic Knight 1.

quest_progression.trigger: Quest for the Toxic God: Stage 4
quest_progression.theme: A Shroud bargain and the cost of recovered memory
quest_progression.causal_summary: The Visitor Hod offers access to the Shroud. The Susurrus demands sensory and emotional prices, and the resulting memory of the Toxic God's ancient visit brings a species-wide sense of loss and apathy.
quest_progression.branching_notes: Hod, the Visitor, and the Susurrus are separate entities; preserve the bargain's price and the negative consequence of the memory.

quest_progression.trigger: Quest for the Toxic God: Stage 5
quest_progression.theme: A challenger tests the Order's honor and equipment
events: The Tale of Knight [Knight 4]: The Challenger
The Tale of Knight [Knight 4]: Passage of Arms
The Tale of Knight [4]: Duty Before Honor
The Tale of Knight [Knight 4]: Honor is All
quest_progression.causal_summary: A stranger defeats several knights and drives a sequence of decisions about challenge, duty, honor, and the Order's prototype neutronium armor.
quest_progression.branching_notes: Preserve the distinction between Knight 4 and the other numbered knights, and retain conditional equipment/reward outcomes.

quest_progression.trigger: Quest for the Toxic God: Stage 6

The Tale of Knight [Knight 10]: The Gatekeeper (3)
The Tale of Knight [10]: The Robot's Disciple
quest_progression.causal_summary: Sinople yields coordinates to an unexplored system, where Knight 10 encounters the Gatekeeper and a robot-linked sequence that continues the Order's pursuit.
quest_progression.branching_notes: The numbered Gatekeeper variants and Robot's Disciple are separate event steps; preserve event order and conditional availability.

The Tale of Knight [Knight 6]: Plea for Help

The Tale of Knight [Knight 6]: The True Visage
quest_progression.causal_summary: Knight 6 receives a three-part mission involving Sinople's trajectory model, prototype armor, and a disappearance. The trail leads to the Trickster and a revelation of the Trickster's true visage.
quest_progression.branching_notes: The Q/R plea variants encode different conditional paths; do not merge them into one text block.

The Tale of Knight [15]: Entering the Station

quest_progression.branching_notes: Keep Witch, station, Syamelle, and the Lover's Pox as separate referents; the event chain's tone is deliberately fairy-tale and dangerous.

quest_progression.trigger: Quest for the Toxic God: Completion
quest_progression.theme: The legendary return and opening the route to the entity
events: The Quest for the Toxic God: The Seal
The Quest for the Toxic God: The Last Trick
The Quest for the Toxic God: Opening the Door
quest_progression.causal_summary: Knight 8 returns from interdimensional travel. The Order recovers the route to the Toxic God, confronts the Trickster, defeats or outlasts the final obstruction, and restores a blocked hyperlane or access route.
quest_progression.branching_notes: The returned Knight 8 is a historical founder and witness, not a newly introduced generic knight; The Seal, Last Trick, and Opening the Door are sequential finale steps.

toxic_entity_events.title: The Quest for the Toxic God: Witnessing Divinity
toxic_entity_events.trigger: First entry into a system containing the Toxic Entity while the empire has Knights of the Toxic God
toxic_entity_events.fact: The knights find a corrosive, metallic, chitinous, tentacled spacefaring entity glowing sick green; the event frames it as the object of the search but does not establish it as the true sentient Toxic God.

toxic_entity_events.title: Toxic Entity
toxic_entity_events.trigger: First entry into the same kind of system without Knights of the Toxic God
toxic_entity_events.fact: The generic encounter identifies a dangerous Toxic Entity without the Order-specific witnessing text.

toxic_entity_events.title: The Quest for the Toxic God: Failure
toxic_entity_events.trigger: First entry when the Toxic Entity is absent or already killed
toxic_entity_events.fact: The trail ends in a system where the entity is gone or was destroyed by another civilization; the Order enters despair and the search for the true God remains unresolved.

toxic_entity_events.title: The Quest for the Toxic God: Trial Overcome
toxic_entity_events.trigger: Defeating the Toxic Entity in battle
toxic_entity_events.fact: The defeated entity can be nursed back to health or used as a weapon; the page lists gaining the Toxic God colossus.

toxic_entity_events.title: The Fate of the Order
toxic_entity_events.trigger: The Quest for the Toxic God: Trial Overcome
toxic_entity_events.fact: Finding the entity removes the Order's purpose, prompting knights to stay or leave and framing the end as an age transition.

toxic_entity_events.title: The Fate of the Toxic God
toxic_entity_events.trigger: The Quest for the Toxic God: Failure or The Quest for the Toxic God: Trial Overcome
toxic_entity_events.fact: The page distinguishes the encountered entity from the original, more formidable and sentient Toxic God, whose trace is associated with the galaxy's central supermassive black hole.

toxic_entity_events.title: Toxic Entity Slain
toxic_entity_events.fact: The entity's venom sack ruptures, its body decomposes, and the Order keeps its maw as a trophy; this confirms the slain creature is not automatically identical to the true Toxic God.

toxic_entity_events.title: Toxic Entity Slain
toxic_entity_events.trigger: A second page-listed variant with a distinct conditional outcome
toxic_entity_events.fact: The duplicate heading is retained because the Wiki exposes two event entries; consumers must not deduplicate solely by display title.

translation_contract: Preserve the numbered knight identities and the Knight A/Knight B roles.
Keep the causal difference between a quest stage trigger, an event choice, a special project completion, and a battle outcome.
Do not translate Toxic Entity as automatically equivalent to Toxic God; this distinction is an explicit endgame fact.
Preserve the order of the eight quests, the final quest, and the separate Toxic Entity events.
Keep conditional branches and duplicate Wiki display headings where they represent distinct event entries.
